problem:
What is the variance of the following data set?

$$
3,\,18,\,11,\,8,\,7,\,18,\,12
$$

Do not round your answer.

${\sigma }^{2}=$
{{field-1}}
worked_solution:
If we have a data set that consists of the points ${x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n},$ then the variance can be computed as

$$
{\sigma }^{2}=\overset{―}{{x}^{2}}-(\overset{―}{x})^{2},
$$

where $\overset{―}{x}$ is the mean of the data set and $\overset{―}{{x}^{2}}$ is the mean of the squares of the points in the data set.

First, let's compute $\overset{―}{x}.$ There are $n=7$ points in our data set, so the mean is

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{―}{x} & =\frac{1}{n}{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i} \\  & =\frac{1}{7}\cdot (3+18+11+8+7+18+12) \\  & =\frac{1}{7}\cdot 77 \\  & =11.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, let's compute $\overset{―}{{x}^{2}}.$ Computing the mean of the squares of the points in the data set, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{―}{{x}^{2}} & =\frac{1}{n}{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i}^{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{7}\cdot ({3}^{2}+{18}^{2}+{11}^{2}+{8}^{2}+{7}^{2}+{18}^{2}+{12}^{2}) \\  & =\frac{1}{7}\cdot (9+324+121+64+49+324+144) \\  & =\frac{1}{7}\cdot 1035 \\  & =\frac{1035}{7}.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the variance is

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sigma }^{2} & =\overset{―}{{x}^{2}}-(\overset{―}{x})^{2} \\  & =\frac{1035}{7}-{(11)}^{2} \\  & =\frac{1035}{7}-121 \\  & =\frac{1035-847}{7} \\  & =\frac{188}{7}.\end{aligned}
$$
